select/fixed: A linear recurrence fades every input by the same a: a name and a comma are forgotten at the same rate.
select/select: Mamba, a selective state space model from 2023, lets each input set its own decay: a t equals e to the minus delta t.
select/delta: Delta t, the step size, comes from x t through a small learned layer, and is always positive.
select/big: A big step forgets: Δ of three gives e to the minus three, about zero point zero five, and the old state is nearly wiped.
select/small: A small step keeps: Δ of zero point one gives about zero point nine, and the state carries on, like an LSTM's forget gate set by the token.
run/h1: With b at one, from zero: step one has nothing to fade, so h one is the input, four.
run/h2: Step two keeps: zero point nine times four, plus two, is five point six.
run/h3: Step three forgets: zero point zero five times five point six is about zero point two eight; add six, and h three is six point two eight, almost all new input.
run/more: Mamba also lets Δ scale the input, and computes b and c from the input too: the token decides what the state keeps.
memory/cache: While generating, a transformer's KV cache holds two, times the layers, times the tokens, times d, times the bytes: it grows with every token.
memory/state: This model keeps only its state, a fixed set of numbers per layer, updated in place: a summary of the past, where the cache keeps every token.
memory/size: Take thirty two layers, d at four thousand, and two bytes per number. At four thousand tokens, the cache is about two gigabytes.
memory/ratio: Give each layer a state of a hundred and twenty eight thousand numbers: about eight megabytes, at any length. The cache is two hundred and fifty times that.
try/p1: Try one: b is one, from zero. Inputs three, five, two; decays zero point five, zero point nine, zero point one. What is h three?
try/a1: Three: a one has nothing to fade. Then two point seven plus five, seven point seven. Then zero point seven seven plus two: two point seven seven.
try/p2: Now both models at eight thousand tokens. How many times the state's memory does the cache take?
try/a2: Per layer, the cache holds two times eight thousand times four thousand numbers; the state, a hundred and twenty eight thousand. Divide: five hundred.
